reason: The SDK sends a plain string when the message is one run of text; we always send content blocks. The API accepts both, and a tool result has no string form, so blocks are the shape our reader and writer share.
The other half of the block list: `{type: "text"}` is what makes a block a block.
The text inside that block. Same string the SDK sends, one level down.

The documented Messages body takes `temperature` at the top level and has for years; anthropic 2.6 moved it under `output_config` in the SDK. Writing the top-level field keeps older endpoints and proxies working. Open question for a live check: whether the API now prefers `output_config`. Worth revisiting, not worth guessing at without a key.
The other side of the same difference.
The SDK puts a role on the system instruction object; the documented `systemInstruction` is `{parts: [...]}` and the role there means nothing. We send the documented shape.
The SDK always sends `tools`, empty when there are none. We omit the key, which the server reads as an empty list.
